findings.title: A sync merge followed by a fast-forward is recorded as a merge-commit landing
findings.description:
The first-parent restriction does not keep sync merges out once the slice branch is fast-forwarded into the target.
- **Flow:** `git merge main` on `381-slice.x` creates S ("Merge branch 'main' into 381-slice.x"). Merging the branch into `main` then fast-forwards by default, so S sits on `main`'s first-parent line.
- **Result:** S matches the pattern's `(^|[^0-9])381-slice` alternative (`src/squadron/review/git_utils.py:234`). It is stored as a `merge_commit` landing with before = a slice-branch commit and tip = old `main`.
- **Knock-on:** because "none found → fast-forward" never fires, the real landing is never recorded.
- **Contradiction:** criterion 1 (line 332) says a sync merge is never taken as a landing. The fixture at line 347 only covers the `--no-ff` variant.
- **Fix:** reject matches whose message merges *into* the slice branch, or require `M^1` to be on the target line independently of `M`. Add a sync-merge-then-fast-forward fixture.

findings.title: The reflog fork is not "the target just before the landing" for a rebased or synced branch
findings.description:
Line 201 claims a fast-forward is only possible if the target had not moved past the fork. That is false after a rebase.
- **Flow:** branch created at A; `main` advances to C; branch is rebased onto C and fast-forwarded.
- **Result:** `_resolve_fork_point` returns the single "branch: Created from" entry, which is still A (`git_utils.py:209-218`). A is an ancestor of the new tip, so the `FORK_NOT_ANCESTOR` check passes.
- **Stored range:** before = A, after = tip, which includes every other slice merged between A and C. D3 exists to exclude exactly that, and the record is permanent.
- **Fixture:** "a rebased branch (`FORK_NOT_ANCESTOR`)" at line 347 will not produce that reason for an ordinary rebase onto an advanced target.
- **Fix:** take `before` from evidence of the landing itself, such as the target's reflog `merge <branch>: Fast-forward` entry or the branch's last `rebase (finish) … onto` entry. Otherwise refuse the landing when the fork is not the target-line parent of the slice's first commit.

findings.title: Every first-parent merge that mentions the slice number becomes a permanent landing
findings.description:
- The architecture accepts the message convention "as the resolver does it today". Today's resolver takes only the newest match (`-1`, `git_utils.py:236`); the design takes all of them.
- `--grep` matches the whole message, not the subject. A later merge whose body says "follow-up to slice 940" becomes a landing of 940.
- A batch-promotion merge on the target line that lists slices becomes a landing of each one. D2 rejects the `main` fallback for this same reason.
- Nothing cross-checks a match against topology, for example `M^2` equal to the branch tip when the branch exists.
- Fix: match the subject only and add a topological check where one is available.

findings.title: A wrong or dead landing can only be removed by hand-deleting the whole project record
findings.description:
- Landings are append-only (D1), and the risk at line 376 admits a wrong one stays.
- The only remedy is deleting the project's file by hand, which also drops every other slice's fast-forward landings whose reflog has expired.
- A landing whose commit was rewritten warns on every report forever (line 165).
- `git cat-file -e` succeeds for unreachable commits until gc, so whether a rewritten landing is measured or shown as "not found" depends on gc state. An ancestor-of-target check would be stable.
- Fix: add a per-slice forget or re-resolve option to `slice-ranges`.

findings.title: An unreadable `slice_ranges` record reads as "no record" and is then overwritten
findings.description:
- Store methods "follow the existing shape" and line 110 specifies a scan. `_iter_records` skips any file that fails to parse or validate with only a WARNING (`src/squadron/metrology/store.py:193-199`).
- `get_slice_ranges` therefore returns `None`, and the next write replaces the file with only the newly resolved landings. Expired fast-forward landings are lost silently.
- The failure table has no row for this.
- "Last write wins" is also not what `_write_atomic` gives. Both writers share one `.tmp` path (`store.py:168`), so a concurrent pair can raise on `replace` or publish a half-written file, which then hits the path above.
- Fix: load by the deterministic id with `load_record`, and treat an existing-but-unreadable record as an error.

findings.title: The `first_parent` argument on `_search_merge_commit` cannot serve the resolver
findings.description:
- The helper returns one abbreviated hash from `--oneline … -1` (`git_utils.py:236-242`).
- The data flow needs every match, oldest first, as full SHAs (line 112), and D1 depends on multiple landings.
- The review resolver is "unchanged", so it will not pass `first_parent` either. The argument has no caller that can use it.
- Line 346 forbids `git_utils.py` growing beyond that argument, so the design does not say where the list-returning search lives.

findings.title: Renaming the helpers breaks the tests the design says pass unchanged
findings.description:
- `tests/review/test_git_utils.py:26-28` imports `_find_merge_commit`, `_find_slice_branch` and `_resolve_fork_point`.
- The same file patches `squadron.review.git_utils._find_slice_branch`, `._resolve_fork_point` and `._search_merge_commit` by string about 30 times, for example at lines 217, 279 and 474.
- `tests/pipeline/test_code_pipelines_branching.py:17` imports `_find_slice_branch`.
- Lines 77 and 386 rename these. Either keep the private names as aliases or state that the tests are updated.

findings.title: A required `environment_root` breaks existing constructors, and `_measure_all` cannot be shared as it stands
findings.description:
- "Required field with no default" (line 211) fails `tests/metrology/snapshot/builders.py:80` and `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_python_length.py:25`, which construct `AdapterContext` without it. "The 400 tests pass unchanged" is false.
- `_measure_all` takes a `PreflightResult` and calls `resolve_files`, which runs `git ls-files` in `repo_root` (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/take.py:93-100`). The export tree is not a repository, and `read_snapshot_config` has no `head_sha`.
- The design does not state the changed signature or the return type of `read_snapshot_config`.

findings.title: Resolver and report git calls have no stated failure handling, and the exit rule conflicts
findings.description:
- The table covers only the reflog read and the merge search. It omits `merge-base(M^1, M^2)`, the two ancestry checks, `cat-file -e` returning `None`, and the first-parent listing behind `report history`.
- A `None` on the fork-ancestor check read as "is an ancestor" persists a landing.
- A target ref that does not exist makes `git log` exit non-zero, and every slice is reported `no_landing`. This happens in a clone that never checked out the integration branch.
- Line 275 says a git error exits 1, while this row says it becomes a reason with exit 0.

findings.title: Reviews with no commit are listed under a slice, against 402's contract
findings.description:
- 402 states that records with `commit_sha is None` or `slice_index is None` roll up at project level only (`project-documents/user/slices/402-slice.code-review-normalization-and-ingest.md:279`).
- The design restates only the `slice_index` half. Lines 150 and 243 select on `slice_index == N` alone.
- 402 counts 37 historical files with no `reviewedSha`. Apply the rule or change 402's contract.

findings.title: `report history` does not say where several kinds of figure go
findings.description:
- Rows are snapshot commits, and this report takes no snapshots.
- Reviews of a resolved slice whose `after_sha` has no snapshot have no row. The closing line excludes them too.
- A slice with two landings (D1's own case) does not say which `after_sha` row carries its reviews.
- Audit runs at commits without a snapshot are not placed.

findings.title: Lint and type figures have no stated sample size
findings.description:
- D8 takes n "from the distribution". Lint and type measurements carry no `distribution` (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/python_lint.py:118-124`, `python_types.py:206-213`).
- The sample output at lines 284-285 shows those rows without n.
- The slice plan requires every figure to carry its sample size. Use `file_count` less `tool_ignored_files`.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 3 cannot run as written
findings.description:
- `sq metrology snapshot --json > a.json` is run from the repo root, and the shell creates `a.json` before the command starts.
- Preflight lists untracked files with `--untracked-files=all` and refuses a dirty tree (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/preflight.py:71`, `150-155`). `.gitignore` does not cover `a.json`.
- Fix: write both files outside the repository.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 2 does not test store durability and leaves a stray record
findings.description:
- `git clone . /tmp/sq-clone` gives the clone an origin that is a filesystem path. `normalize_remote_url` passes it through as the project id (`src/squadron/metrology/identity.py:119-123`).
- The clone therefore reads no stored record and writes a second `sliceranges-*` file in the real user store.
- The step proves topology only, not the claim at line 176.
- No walkthrough step covers criterion 2: a fast-forward slice persisted, then resolved with the branch deleted.

findings.title: The 401 cache claim is not supported by what 401 says
findings.description: 401 describes a reader built per registry whose first call does the work and later calls return the cached reading (401:91-97). I found no statement that the cache is keyed on `repo_root`. `report slice` takes several exports under one registry. The effect is nil while coverage is absent at every export.

findings.title: Smaller export gaps
findings.description:
- "Tools run with `cwd=repo_root`" and "the uv check from `environment_root`" conflict for uv. `resolve_environment` checks lock and venv under one root and runs uv there (`python_types.py:72-93`). State that uv runs in the live checkout.
- The in-place-equals-export test cannot detect the editable-install leak, because the two trees are identical at HEAD. Step 4 has no reference value for an old commit (line 380).
- The 30 s `git archive` bound is a constant in the review module (`git_utils.py:25`), with no setting for a large brownfield repo.
- A tracked symlink pointing outside the tree makes a commit permanently unexportable (line 161), although only regular files are measured.
- Line 315 names a `landings` field that the schema does not have.
